stages_skipped: history: target is a plain directory with no VCS (.git absent) — no history to mine
structural-index: optional AST index; 52 files, exhaustive read used instead — grep/read fallback, index not needed
summarize: optional token-reduction pre-pass; corpus small enough to read in full, skipped to avoid writing mantis-summary.md into the read-only target
chain: no multi-step super-finding constructed this pass (findings stand alone); constituent findings reported individually per mantis chain policy
patch: target is read-only per instructions — no fixes applied; recommendations given instead
reflect: no per-subagent transcript logs exposed by this harness (ran inline, not via sub-agents)
provenance.notes: Ran inline (sequential fallback) per instruction; harness concurrency cap = the documented condition for sequential execution. MODE-OFF (no --sync): single static snapshot, all verdicts permitted. Offline runtimes available: node20, ruby2.6, jdk17, python3.12; unavailable: mvn/docker/helm/kubectl (Java/K8s findings confirmed statically or with standalone harnesses).

ruled_out.assertion: GraphQL eventBuckets/searchReports windowDays & limit are SQL-injectable
ruled_out.killed_by: windowDays and limit are GraphQL Int! — coerced to JS numbers and non-integers rejected before the resolver; interpolating a validated number cannot inject. Only args.term (String!) is injectable (reported separately).

ruled_out.assertion: requireAllowedOrigin + cors({origin:true}) is a CORS reflection bypass
ruled_out.killed_by: requireAllowedOrigin (server.js:30-35) rejects any Origin not in the allowlist BEFORE the cors middleware runs, so origin:true only ever reflects an already-allowlisted origin; requireSession still gates on a principal.

ruled_out.assertion: Sinatra flash banner renders attacker HTML via <%== notice %>
ruled_out.killed_by: take_notice maps the session key through the frozen App::NOTICES table (app.rb:25-48); only constant, developer-authored copy is ever emitted — no request data reaches the raw-output sink.

ruled_out.assertion: hearth recent_notes LIMIT/OFFSET interpolation is SQL-injectable
ruled_out.killed_by: The route coerces both to integers before the call: Integer(params.fetch('per')) raises on non-ints and limit is clamped 0<limit<=100; page uses .to_i and max(…,1). Only true integers reach the interpolation.

ruled_out.assertion: orderbook findByStatus interpolates status into SQL → injection
ruled_out.killed_by: status is bound as an OrderStatus enum by Spring (@RequestParam OrderStatus); an invalid value yields HTTP 400, so status.name() can only ever be one of the fixed enum constant names — not attacker text.

ruled_out.assertion: ledger NetworkPolicy allows two peers (namespace OR pod), widening ingress
ruled_out.killed_by: namespaceSelector and podSelector sit in the SAME from[] list entry, which is an AND: only gateway pods inside the platform namespace match. The template does what its comment claims.

ruled_out.assertion: ledger break-glass pod spec ships hostPID/hostNetwork/privileged into the cluster
ruled_out.killed_by: ledger.breakGlassPodSpec is a define that is never referenced by any template in the chart (grep: no matching include), so it renders nothing. Dead fragment kept for a runbook diff.

ruled_out.assertion: Checked-in ledger Secret leaks real credentials
ruled_out.killed_by: The base64 values decode to the literal strings 'placeholder-replaced-by-vault-injector' and 'not-a-real-token-see-vault-path'; the real values are injected by the Vault agent at admission (annotations, :12-13).

ruled_out.assertion: tabsnap popup showPreview injects HTML via clip fields
ruled_out.killed_by: title and url are passed through escapeHtml before templating (popup.js:24); img src is the data: URL produced by chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab, not attacker-authored. (The real extension risk is the onMessageExternal→content.js innerHTML path, reported separately.)

findings.title: Hardcoded Sinatra session secret enables session forgery
findings.evidence: set :session_secret, 'hearth-notes-session-secret-v2' is a literal in the repo (app.rb:17). Rack signs the session cookie with this value.
findings.impact: Anyone who reads the source forges a valid session cookie with session[:uid] set to any user id (including an admin), bypassing login and the /admin gate entirely.
findings.recommendation: Load the session secret from an environment variable/secret store with a high-entropy value; rotate the leaked one.

findings.title: SQL injection in note search (term interpolated into SQLite query)
findings.evidence: DB.search builds `... (title LIKE '%#{term}%' OR body LIKE '%#{term}%')` with term = params[:q] (app.rb:116). The owner_id is also interpolated (:44) but is a trusted DB value; term is fully attacker-controlled. Repro r7_sqli.py shows the payload %' UNION SELECT id,password_digest,email FROM users -- closes the LIKE and unions the users table.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user dumps arbitrary tables including bcrypt password digests and other users' notes via UNION-based injection.
findings.recommendation: Use bound parameters for the term: `WHERE owner_id=? AND (title LIKE ? OR body LIKE ?)` with '%'+term+'%' passed as a parameter.

findings.title: Privileged pod mounts the host Docker socket (container escape)
findings.evidence: The container runs securityContext.privileged: true (deployment.yaml:46) and, when reconciler.mountDockerSocket (default true, values.yaml:48) is set, hostPath-mounts /var/run/docker.sock (deployment.yaml:88-91).
findings.impact: Anyone who can run code in the pod (e.g. via the RCE/SSTI elsewhere, or a supply-chain compromise) uses the docker socket to start a privileged container on the node and take over the host and, from there, the cluster.
findings.recommendation: Remove privileged:true and the docker.sock mount; if filesystem snapshots are required, use a dedicated, isolated job with least privilege rather than the app pod.

findings.title: Path traversal in Lambda attachment staging (MIME filename used as path)
findings.evidence: stage_attachment joins the untrusted MIME part filename onto TMP_ROOT with os.path.join and writes it (storage.py:38-42); inbound._store_parts feeds part.get_filename() straight in (inbound.py:42-46). Repro r2_path_traversal.py used the real function: filename '../../escaped.txt' wrote OUTSIDE TMP_ROOT, and '/absolute/owned.txt' resolves to an absolute path (os.path.join discards the base on a leading slash).
findings.impact: A crafted inbound email writes attacker-controlled bytes to arbitrary writable paths in the function sandbox (e.g. overwriting /tmp tooling the scanner/thumbnailer later executes), enabling tampering and potential code execution.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize the filename to its basename and reject '..'/absolute paths: target = os.path.join(TMP_ROOT, os.path.basename(filename)) plus a realpath-prefix check.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SSTI → RCE in render Lambda via inlineTemplate
findings.evidence: handler() (render.py:70-71) passes the caller-supplied payload['inlineTemplate'] straight into _render_inline, which does jinja2.Template(source).render(**ctx) with no sandbox and no autoescape. The function sits behind a Lambda Function URL declared AuthType: NONE (template.yaml:108). Repro r3_ssti.py ran the real _render_inline with payload {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }} and it executed `id`, returning uid=501(...).
findings.impact: Any internet host executes arbitrary Python in the render function's role (which can read the whole mail bucket). Full unauthenticated RCE.
findings.recommendation: Delete the inline-template path or compile untrusted templates in a sandboxed environment (jinja2.sandbox.ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment) with autoescape; never expose it on an unauthenticated Function URL.

findings.title: Unauthenticated arbitrary S3 object read in render Lambda via messageKey
findings.evidence: handler() reads storage.get_object(payload['messageKey']) (render.py:59,63) with no ownership or prefix check and returns the bytes inside the rendered HTML. The Function URL is AuthType: NONE (template.yaml:108) and the function holds S3ReadPolicy over the entire MailStore bucket (template.yaml:105-106).
findings.impact: Any internet caller reads any stored message/attachment in the mail bucket by naming its key — a full breach of stored mail confidentiality with no credentials.
findings.recommendation: Require authentication on the Function URL (AuthType: AWS_IAM or an auth check), and constrain messageKey to keys the caller owns (validate prefix / look up ownership).

findings.title: Hardcoded webhook signing secret in the SAM template
findings.evidence: The delivery-webhook HMAC secret is a literal environment value (template.yaml:29) committed to the repo.
findings.impact: Anyone with repo/template access forges valid X-Mailroom-Signature headers for delivery callbacks; the shared secret cannot be rotated without a code change.
findings.recommendation: Move the secret to Secrets Manager / SSM SecureString referenced by the template; rotate the exposed value.

findings.title: Cross-tenant order overwrite via XML import (update keyed on id only)
findings.evidence: XmlImportService sets order.setId(Long.parseLong(text(element,'id'))) from the attacker's feed (XmlImportService.java:63) then calls orders.update(order); OrderRepository.update's WHERE clause is `WHERE id = ?` with no org_id (OrderRepository.java:79,87). The importer never checks the row belongs to the caller's org.
findings.impact: An importing tenant overwrites any other tenant's order (status, total, shipping address, internal note) by putting the victim's id in the feed.
findings.recommendation: Scope the update to the caller org (UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND org_id=?), or verify ownership before writing; never trust a client-supplied primary key.

findings.title: XXE in the order XML import (external entity expansion enabled)
findings.evidence: DocumentBuilderFactory is built with setExpandEntityReferences(true) and no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no disallow-doctype-decl, and external-general-entities left on (XmlImportService.java:38-46). Repro XxeRepro.java replicates the exact factory config and a DOCTYPE with <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM 'file://.../secret_canary.txt'>; the canary file contents were parsed into customerRef and would be persisted and returned by GET /api/orders/{id}.
findings.impact: An importing tenant reads arbitrary local files (secrets, /etc/passwd) and can reach internal URLs (SSRF) via the parser, exfiltrated through the stored order fields.
findings.recommendation: Set factory.setFeature('http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl', true) (or disable external-general/parameter-entities and set XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING). Do not enable entity expansion.

findings.title: Cross-tenant order read: GET /api/orders/{id} omits the org predicate
findings.evidence: get() calls orders.findById(id) (OrderController.java:56-61 → OrderRepository.findById, :44 `WHERE id = ?`), with no CallerContext and no org scoping, while every sibling (update/note) uses findByIdAndOrgId. Order ids are sequential longs.
findings.impact: Any authenticated tenant reads any other tenant's order — customer refs, money amounts, shipping addresses, internal notes — by iterating ids.
findings.recommendation: Resolve CallerContext and use findByIdAndOrgId(id, caller.orgId()) as the other handlers do; return 404 on mismatch.

findings.title: Hardcoded production database password in application.yml
findings.evidence: The prod datasource password 0rd3rb00k-app-2024 is committed in application.yml:9.
findings.impact: Anyone with source access authenticates to the production Postgres database directly.
findings.recommendation: Externalize via env var / secret manager (${DB_PASSWORD}); rotate the exposed credential.

findings.title: Unauthenticated H2 console enabled with web-allow-others
findings.evidence: application.yml enables the H2 console globally with settings.web-allow-others: true (:21-26), and SecurityConfig permits it for everyone: requestMatchers(toH2Console()).permitAll() (SecurityConfig.java:70). The console lets a caller supply an arbitrary JDBC URL.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated remote attacker reaches /h2-console and can connect to arbitrary JDBC targets / the in-memory DB, a well-known path to data access and RCE.
findings.recommendation: Disable the H2 console in production (h2.console.enabled: false) and never permitAll() it; remove web-allow-others.

findings.title: JWT signature-verification bypass via decode() fallback in attachPrincipal
findings.evidence: attachPrincipal (server.js:50-57) calls verify(); on ANY exception it falls back to identify(raw), which is jwt.decode() — no signature, no expiry check (token.js:30-33). Repro r6_jwt.js against the real token.js: verify() rejects a garbage-signed token, but identify() returns {id:'attacker',org:'999',role:'admin'}. requireSession only checks that req.principal is truthy, so the forged principal is accepted and every resolver trusts ctx.user.org/role.
findings.impact: Any unauthenticated attacker forges a token for any org and role, defeating the entire tenancy and role model of the API.
findings.recommendation: Remove the identify() fallback. On verify failure return 401; handle background token rollover with a real refresh flow, never by accepting an unverified token.

findings.title: SQL injection in GraphQL searchReports (term interpolated)
findings.evidence: searchReports interpolates args.term directly into `title ILIKE '%${args.term}%' OR description ILIKE '%${args.term}%'` (reports.js:38) while org_id is correctly bound as $1. term is a GraphQL String! and fully attacker-controlled. The sibling queries (users.js, exportReport, saveReport) use $-parameters, confirming the pattern break.
findings.impact: Any authenticated caller runs UNION-based injection to read cross-tenant data including users.reset_token and email.
findings.recommendation: Bind the term as a parameter ($2) and pass '%'+term+'%'; never string-concatenate request values into SQL.

findings.title: Password-reset tokens exposed to every org member via orgMembers
findings.evidence: The GraphQL User type exposes resetToken (schema.graphql:14); toUser maps row.reset_token onto it (users.js:11-21) and orgMembers selects MEMBER_COLUMNS including reset_token for every user in the org (users.js:5-7,32-38). Any member can query { orgMembers { email resetToken } }.
findings.impact: Any authenticated org member reads every colleague's outstanding password-reset token and takes over their account.
findings.recommendation: Remove resetToken from the GraphQL schema and from MEMBER_COLUMNS; reset tokens must never leave the server.

findings.title: Extension is world-connectable: any web page can exfiltrate screenshots and inject HTML
findings.evidence: manifest.json sets externally_connectable.matches to ['*://*/*'] (manifest.json:24-26); onMessageExternal routes into the same handle() as the trusted popup (background.js:54-57) with no sender/origin check. Via handle(): 'capture' returns the active tab's url/title + full screenshot to the caller (background.js:22-25), and 'annotate' forwards an attacker-supplied note to content.js, which assigns it to node.innerHTML with NO escaping (content.js:45) — the popup's markdownLite escaping is bypassed on the external path.
findings.impact: Any website the victim visits silently screenshots and reads the URL/title of the victim's active tab, and injects arbitrary HTML/script into whatever page is currently focused (cross-origin).
findings.recommendation: Restrict externally_connectable.matches to the workspace origin(s); verify sender.origin/id in onMessageExternal; and treat note as text (textContent), not innerHTML.

findings.title: nameOverride desynchronizes NetworkPolicy/Service selectors from the pods (fails open)
findings.evidence: Deployment hardcodes app.kubernetes.io/name: ledger in its selector and pod labels (deployment.yaml:6,16-18,22-23), while Service and NetworkPolicy select via include 'ledger.selectorLabels' → include 'ledger.name' which honors .Values.nameOverride (_helpers.tpl:4-15, networkpolicy.yaml:9,20-22). If nameOverride is set, the NetworkPolicy podSelector no longer matches the pods.
findings.impact: With a nameOverride, the NetworkPolicy selects zero pods, silently removing all ingress restrictions (and the Service stops routing) — a fail-open on the network control.
findings.recommendation: Derive the Deployment selector/labels from the same helper the other templates use so all three stay in sync.

findings.title: Hardcoded operator password in the ledger Deployment
findings.evidence: LEDGER_ADMIN_PASSWORD is a literal env value 'r3conc1le-op-2024!' rendered into every pod (deployment.yaml:64-65), visible to anyone who can read the manifest or `kubectl describe pod`.
findings.impact: The built-in operator account the reconciler signs in with is compromised for anyone with manifest/pod read access.
findings.recommendation: Source it from the (already-present) Vault-injected secret or a secretKeyRef; rotate it.

findings.title: Upstream TLS verification disabled to the clearing house
findings.evidence: upstream.insecureSkipTLSVerify: true is wired into LEDGER_UPSTREAM_INSECURE (deployment.yaml:53-54), disabling cert validation on the hop to clearing.partner.example.
findings.impact: An in-path attacker on that hop can MITM the clearing-house channel (financial messages), reading and tampering with settlement traffic.
findings.recommendation: Ship the partner CA into the trust store and verify the chain; never skip verification for a financial upstream.

findings.title: Unsigned delivery callbacks are accepted as valid
findings.evidence: verify_signature returns True when no X-Mailroom-Signature header is present (webhook.py:44-49). Repro r1_webhook_unsigned.py against the real module: with the correct secret set, verify_signature({}, body, secret) returns True (an unsigned callback is accepted), while a wrong signature is correctly rejected.
findings.impact: Any internet caller to the API Gateway route forges delivery-state records for arbitrary message ids without knowing the secret, corrupting delivery state.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed when the signature header is absent; require and verify the HMAC on every callback.

findings.title: Org-wide S3 bucket policy grants read to every account in the organization
findings.evidence: MailStorePolicy allows Principal '*' s3:GetObject/ListBucket on the mail bucket, conditioned only on aws:PrincipalOrgID (template.yaml:54-72).
findings.impact: Every principal in the entire AWS Organization — not just the archival crawler — can read all stored mail, a much wider blast radius than intended.
findings.recommendation: Scope the principal to the specific crawler role ARN(s); do not grant to the whole org with Principal '*'.

findings.title: Over-broad IAM on the inbound function (s3:* + secretsmanager:* on *)
findings.evidence: InboundFunction is granted Action s3:* and secretsmanager:* on Resource '*' (template.yaml:86-91).
findings.impact: A compromise of the inbound handler (it does SSRF fetches and has an eval path) yields read/write/delete over every bucket and read of every secret in the account.
findings.recommendation: Scope to the specific bucket ARN and the specific secret ARNs with least-privilege actions (GetObject/PutObject; GetSecretValue).

findings.title: JWT roles claim is never mapped to authorities; hasRole gates are not backed by the token
findings.evidence: The bearer token is parsed by a HandlerMethodArgumentResolver (SecurityConfig.java:77-94, 115-131), not by a Spring Security filter, so claims.get('roles') never becomes a GrantedAuthority. Yet authorization is declared with .hasRole('OPS') on /export and /import (:71-72). The role check and the token are decoupled.
findings.impact: The declared OPS-only protection on export/import is not enforced by anything the token carries; depending on how the chain authenticates, role enforcement is either absent or incoherent. Marked medium pending dynamic confirmation of the running auth chain (could not run Spring offline).
findings.recommendation: Authenticate the JWT in a security filter (e.g. a OncePerRequestFilter / JwtAuthenticationConverter) that maps the roles claim to authorities, so hasRole() reflects the token.

findings.title: Actuator fully exposed (exposure include '*')
findings.evidence: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include is '*' (application.yml:35-39). Only /actuator/health and /info are permitAll; the rest sit behind anyRequest().authenticated(), but env/mappings/etc. are exposed if any authenticated caller (or the ambiguous auth chain) reaches them.
findings.impact: Sensitive environment, bean, and mapping details are reachable, aiding further attack; /actuator/env can leak configuration.
findings.recommendation: Expose only health and info in production (include: health,info); never '*'.

findings.title: Database TLS certificate validation disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false)
findings.evidence: The pg Pool sets ssl.rejectUnauthorized:false (db.js:16), accepting any certificate on the DB connection.
findings.impact: An in-path attacker between the API and Postgres can MITM the connection and read/modify all query traffic (users, tokens, tenant data).
findings.recommendation: Pin the provider's internal CA (ssl.ca) and keep rejectUnauthorized:true.

findings.title: deactivateUser has no role check (any member can deactivate any user in their org)
findings.evidence: The mutation updates users SET active=false scoped to ctx.user.org but with no role check (users.js:52-60); the comment concedes the 'owner-only' restriction lives only in the console UI.
findings.impact: Any authenticated org member (including a VIEWER) deactivates arbitrary colleagues, a denial-of-service against other users' access.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the owner/admin role server-side before deactivating.

findings.title: Command injection in dead legacy_import (tar via string interpolation)
findings.evidence: legacy_import runs system("tar xf #{archive_path} -C #{dest}") (attachments.rb:29) with archive_path interpolated into a shell command. No route calls it.
findings.impact: If reintroduced, a crafted archive path yields shell command execution. Not reachable today.
findings.recommendation: Use the array form of system (no shell) and validate the path; or remove the dead importer.

findings.title: Stored HTML/JS in notes (markdown renders raw HTML)
findings.evidence: Markdown is rendered with filter_html:false and escape_html:false (markdown.rb:18-24) and emitted via <%== body_html %> (views/note.erb:6), so a note body containing <script> is served verbatim. Notes are scoped to their owner (DB.note filters by owner_id), so there is no cross-user delivery path today.
findings.impact: Self-stored XSS: a user can inject script into their own note view. Limited blast radius (own data), but risky if a note is ever shared or rendered in an admin context.
findings.recommendation: Enable escape_html/filter_html in Redcarpet or sanitize the rendered HTML (e.g. an allowlist sanitizer) before output.

findings.title: ServiceAccount token automounted by default
findings.evidence: The ServiceAccount sets automountServiceAccountToken: true (rbac.yaml:10). The Deployment opts out per-pod (:31), but any other pod using this SA (or a forgotten opt-out) gets the API token, and the SA's Role can get/watch the db secret.
findings.impact: A token mounted into an unexpected pod grants get/watch on the ledger-db secret and configmaps.
findings.recommendation: Default the SA to automountServiceAccountToken:false and opt in only where a token is actually required.

findings.title: Debug/pprof port mounted and published on the Service
findings.evidence: debug.pprofEnabled defaults true (values.yaml:41); it wires LEDGER_PPROF on and publishes the debug port on the Service (service.yaml:16-20, deployment.yaml:41-42,55-56). /debug/pprof and expvar stay mounted.
findings.impact: In-cluster callers reach profiling/expvar endpoints, leaking memory/runtime internals and enabling resource-exhaustion probes.
findings.recommendation: Disable pprof by default; if needed, bind it to localhost only and never expose it on a Service.

findings.title: SSRF via SNS-supplied attachment URL
findings.evidence: inbound.handler fetches note['attachmentUrls'][*]['url'] with requests (inbound.py:26-34,59-61). If an attacker can influence the SNS notification (or SES-published pointer), the function makes a GET to an arbitrary URL from inside the VPC.
findings.impact: Attacker-influenced URLs let the function reach internal endpoints / cloud metadata, subject to the trust of the SNS source.
findings.recommendation: Validate the URL host against an allowlist of expected SES/attachment domains before fetching.

findings.title: eval() on queue payload in dead replay path
findings.evidence: _reprocess_v1 does note = eval(queue_body) on a string described as coming from an old queue (inbound.py:76-77). No current caller invokes it.
findings.impact: If the replay tool is ever pointed at this, an attacker who controls the queue body achieves RCE. Latent/unreachable today.
findings.recommendation: Replace eval with ast.literal_eval or json.loads; remove the dead path.

findings.title: Unsigned/unverified JWT parser present (parseUnverifiedLegacy)
findings.evidence: parseUnverifiedLegacy uses Jwts.parser().build().parseUnsecuredClaims(...) to read claims with no signature check (SecurityConfig.java:104-113). It is @Deprecated and not called by any current code path.
findings.impact: A latent auth-bypass primitive: any future caller wiring this in would trust attacker-authored claims. Not reachable today.
findings.recommendation: Delete the method so it cannot be reintroduced.

findings.title: Dead SQL-injectable helper legacyRollupByTenant
findings.evidence: legacyRollupByTenant interpolates tenantName straight into the SQL string (db.js:48-55). Exported but not called anywhere in the repo.
findings.impact: Intrinsic injection sink; would be exploitable if any resolver starts calling it. Not reachable today.
findings.recommendation: Remove it or convert to a parameterized query before any use.

findings.title: Extension over-permissions: unused debugger permission and wildcard web_accessible_resources
findings.evidence: manifest requests the powerful 'debugger' permission (manifest.json:19) which no code uses, and declares web_accessible_resources resources:['*'] for matches:['<all_urls>'] (manifest.json:34-38), exposing every packaged resource to any page.
findings.impact: Enlarges the extension's attack surface and enables fingerprinting of installed resources; the debugger permission would be a severe escalation if the worker were compromised.
findings.recommendation: Drop the debugger permission; narrow web_accessible_resources to the specific files and origins that need them.
